item.title: Prep girls basketball: American Canyon steals the show on Senior Night
item.description: Four different players finished in double figures as the Wolves forced 23 steals and scored a season-high 81 points in an 81-15 thrashing of Petaluma on Wednesday night.

item.title: Danette Mitchell: On Black History Month, a look at ‘Uncle Tom’
item.description: Uncle Tom’s character was humble, nonviolent, and displayed strong Christian values, including acts of self-sacrifice. Many would say to the extreme.

item.title: Six Flags Discovery Kingdom giraffe says Super Bowl winner is …
item.description: In a yearly tradition in which Six Flags Discovery Kingdom bestows the honor of letting an animal choose this year’s Super Bowl winner, this year, Chich the two and a half year old giraffe, was the lucky mammal.

item.title: Elwood Watson: Trump’s war against Black history
item.description: No amount of perverse revisionism or fierce efforts to whitewash the stoic, powerful, and esteemed history of a fiercely impervious and undeniably resilient people will succeed.

item.title: Republicans reject complaint about Gabbard as Democrats question time it took to see it
item.description: The top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee said he will keep looking into it.

item.title: Census Bureau plans to use survey with a citizenship question in its test for 2030, alarming experts

item.title: Local cardiologist sounds alarm on women’s hearts
item.description: As Heart Health Month continues, cardiologists are urging women to pay closer attention to a risk that’s often misunderstood — heart disease, the leading cause of death for women. “Awareness is the best thing we can do,” said Dr. Leila Ganjehei, M.D., a cardiologist at Kaiser Vallejo Medical Center. “In medicine, and especially at Kaiser, our goal is to prevent more than we treat.” Many women still associate heart disease primarily with men, but the reality is far different, says Dr. Ganjehei. “
